facts.text: Eddystone was named after the Eddystone Lighthouse in England, thanks to founder William Simpson’s admiration for the sea‑sheltered beacon.
The borough’s roots trace back to 1641 when Swedish settlers, led by Olof Stille, first occupied the land that would become Eddystone.
In the 1840s, William Simpson established a textile print works that would become the heart of the town’s industrial growth.
The tenement blocks built for print‑works workers are now known as “The Village,” a historic neighborhood that still lines the town center.
Eddystone’s riverfront once hosted a power plant that opened in 1960 and is now operated by Exelon, reflecting the town’s shift from textiles to energy.
The Delaware River shapes Eddystone’s landscape, with tidal estuary dynamics influencing local drainage and occasional flooding events.
